## Purpose

List pages in this dashboard do not render a flat table; they bucket rows into labelled sections — Activity groups sessions by work kind, Sessions groups them by category, Knowledge splits real knowledge from measured friction. The `*Section` type is the page-local contract between a pure grouping function and the render loop: a stable key, a display label, and the rows. Keeping the grouping pure and memoised means the ordering rules (priority buckets first, the null bucket last, the attribution-leak rows at the tail) live in one readable place instead of being smeared across JSX.

## Convention

Folder: apps/dashboard/src/pages/** · Extension: .tsx · Files of this role in this subproject: 3

- The bucket type is a page-local, NOT exported `interface <Page>Section { key: string; label: string; <rows>: T[] }` — `ActivitySection` in `Activity.tsx` and `SessionSection` in `Sessions.tsx` are the same three fields over `SessionRow[]`.
- It is produced by one pure function declared right below it (`groupByKind`, `groupSessions`) returning `<Page>Section[] | undefined`. `undefined` is the deliberate "still loading" signal — both return early when `data` is undefined — so the page can distinguish loading from a genuinely empty list.
- Bucketing uses a `new Map<string, T[]>` fill, then an explicit sort over `[...buckets.keys()]`: a module-level `PRIORITY_ORDER` array pins the leading buckets, a `NULL_BUCKET` sentinel is forced last, and everything else falls back to `localeCompare` on the label. Within a bucket the backend's arrival order is preserved, with the special rows pushed to the tail.
- The page memoises the call: `const sections = useMemo(() => groupSessions(data), [data])` — Activity passes the translator into the grouping and lists it in the deps (`[data, t]`) because labels are resolved there.
- Rendering is `<div className="flex flex-col gap-6">` over the sections, each a `<SectionHeader title={section.label} right={…count} />` from `@/components/page` followed by a `<DataCard>` wrapping a `<ul>` of row components — no bespoke section chrome.
- The page distinguishes three states explicitly: no project (`EmptyState` inside `PageSurface`), `sections.length === 0` (a different `EmptyState` with its own copy), and loaded.
- Labels come from the i18n helper (`useT()` in `Activity.tsx` and `Knowledge.tsx`); `Sessions.tsx` uses a local `CATEGORY_LABELS` map with a capitalise fallback for unmapped values instead — prefer the i18n route on new pages.
- A section that owns real rendering logic becomes its own page-local component taking its data as a prop (`FrictionSection({ friction })` in `Knowledge.tsx`), still unexported, with a doc comment explaining why the section is kept separate from its neighbours.

## How to apply

Add the interface, the grouping function and the priority constants near the bottom of the page file, above the page's exported component. Return `undefined` while data is undefined, keep the function pure (pass `t` in rather than calling a hook inside), memoise the call in the component, and render through `SectionHeader` + `DataCard`. Do not export the section type — if two pages need the same grouping, lift the row type to `src/lib` and the rendering to `@/components/page` instead of sharing the page-local bucket.

## Examples

- Ref: apps/dashboard/src/pages/Activity.tsx — `ActivitySection` + `groupByKind(data, t)` with `PRIORITY_ORDER`, the null bucket last, and the leak rows sorted to the tail.
- Ref: apps/dashboard/src/pages/Sessions.tsx — `SessionSection` + `groupSessions(data)`, then the `SectionHeader`/`DataCard`/`<ul>` render loop.
- Ref: apps/dashboard/src/pages/Knowledge.tsx — the component form: `FrictionSection` as an unexported section component with its own `SectionHeader` and empty state.
